correctness.rationale: For D=z(P-z^d)Πell_j with P=Πell_j^{k_j} and distinct linear forms, the nonlinear component is smooth away from z=0 because ∂_z(P-z^d)=-dz^{d-1}; added lines cannot meet it there. At q=[0:0:1] the m lines form an ordinary m-fold point with tau=(m-1)^2 and lct=min(1,2/m)=2/m. At each p_j=(z=ell_j=0), the other line factors are analytic units; taking a holomorphic k_j-th root of their product reduces the germ to uv(u^{k_j}-v^d). It is reduced weighted homogeneous with weights d,k_j and weighted degree dk_j+d+k_j, giving mu=tau=(d+1)(k_j+1) and lct=(d+k_j)/(dk_j+d+k_j). Since phi_d'(k)=-d^2/(dk+d+k)^2<0, only K=max_j k_j controls the global lct. Total tau=(m-1)^2+(d+1)(d+m) equals the expected free-curve value for degree d+m+1 and exponents (m-1,d+1). The d=6,m=3 partition comparison is exactly 2/5 versus 5/17. An independent weighted-Euler and symbolic check passed, corroborative to the local geometric argument.
residual_risks: All ℓ_j must remain pairwise nonproportional, k_j positive, over C; no formula is asserted for arbitrary free curves.
